findings.comment: In C, parentheses around comma-separated expressions invoke the comma operator rather than passing multiple arguments to `snprintf`. Consequently, `snprintf` only receives three arguments (`buf`, `sizeof(buf)`, and the evaluated result of the ternary expression as the format string). When `server.hide_user_data_from_log` is non-zero, the format string receives `sdslen(c->querybuf) - c->qb_pos` (a size_t integer cast to a pointer), causing an immediate segmentation fault. When `server.hide_user_data_from_log` is 0, the format string receives the end of `c->querybuf` (user-controlled data) with no further arguments, introducing a critical format string vulnerability.
